title: What the Credited Proportion Acts On in a Temporary Dispute Credit
content:
What the credited proportion acts on, when a temporary credit is sized on a card under Personal Credit Cards, turns on the money the cardholder moves through Personal Checking and on whether Personal Checking has charged them a fee.

*Where Piedmont Crescent Bank checking deposits posted to the cardholder's checking accounts in the last six months total at least 12000.00 USD and no Piedmont Crescent Bank checking fee was posted to those accounts in the last six months* — the credited proportion acts on the amount claimed together with the card fees posted to the card account in the last two months.

*Where those deposits total at least 12000.00 USD and at least one Piedmont Crescent Bank checking fee was posted to those accounts in the last six months* — the credited proportion acts on the amount claimed together with the most recent card fee posted to the card account.

*Where those deposits total less than 12000.00 USD* — the credited proportion acts on the amount claimed alone.

**What each convention is worth.** On a hypothetical amount claimed of 200.00 USD, a card account carrying card fees of 32.00 USD and then 41.00 USD posted in the last two months, the later of the two being the 41.00 USD, and a credited proportion of 70 percent: the first convention acts on 273.00 USD and gives 191.10 USD; the second acts on 241.00 USD, taking the most recent card fee alone, and gives 168.70 USD; the third acts on 200.00 USD and gives 140.00 USD.

**On the boundaries.** The deposit figure is read as at least, so deposits of exactly 12000.00 USD in the last six months belong with the higher band, and 11999.00 USD with the lower. Where the deposits fall short, the count of checking fees does not come into it at all.
